source.title: Efficacy of steroid therapy for Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy

consistency_findings: Table 6 shows decreased salivation in patients 3, 4, and 8 (3/9), whereas the discussion states that two cases achieved decreased salivation. Both assertions are retained separately and marked needs_review.

Table 6 shows increased vocabulary in patient 9 only (1/9), whereas the discussion states that two cases attained increased vocabulary. Both assertions are retained separately and marked needs_review.

The Results text reports mean steroid administration duration as 8.86 months with SD 3.05 years, while Table 3 presents 8.86 (3.05 SD) under a months column. The apparent unit inconsistency was not normalized into an atom.

The discussion says motor functions improved in all nine patients, whereas Figure 1 shows total GMFM score decreased in patient 3; the article notes that patient 3 nevertheless improved in GMFM dimension A. The atom set preserves the specific Figure 1 results rather than converting the broad discussion wording into a total-score claim.
extraction_limitations: The PDF references a Supplemental Protocol 1, but no supplement was present in the retrieved Drive folder; supplement-dependent details were not invented.
This is a single-arm, open-label study; the atom extraction records reported findings and does not treat causal efficacy as established.
Figure 1 patient-level GMFM values were visually reconciled against the rendered PDF and normalized into patient-level quantitative atoms.
